diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since the eigenvalues of $Z^TGZ$ are all positive \cite{horn2013matrix}, and using the fact that $Z^T=Z^{-1}$ we can reformulate this problem as follows:
we let $H =ZY$, where $Z$ is a projection to the null space of $F^T$ and $Z^TZ=I$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims the fair maximization of Tr(H^T G H) (which for G=A_sym+2I is the fair NCut relaxation (mainobj)) has the same maximizer as the fair minimization of Tr(H^T G^{-1} H). The only justification is 'Z^T = Z^{-1}', but Z is n×(n-h+1) and has no inverse; in general (Z^T G Z)^{-1} ≠ Z^T G^{-1} Z. Counterexample: G=diag(1,2,10), F=(1,1,1)^T, k=1: the top eigenvector of Z^T G Z is approximately (-0.05,1) in the basis z1=(1,-1,0)/√2, z2=(1,1,-2)/√6, while the bottom eigenvector of Z^T G^{-1} Z is approximately (-0.30,1); the constrained maximizers differ. The subsequent SMW/limit derivation and U = G - GF(F^TGF)^{-1}F^TG = Z(Z^TG^{-1}Z)^{-1}Z^T actually solve (SMW2), so Fair-SMW optimizes the fair-constrained Tr(H^T G^{-1} H), not the fair spectral relaxation (mainobj) it is advertised to reformulate.

failure_location.quote: Notice that \eqref{SMW2} is equivalent to \eqref{SMW1} in the sense that the maximizer $H$ is the same.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must withdraw the equivalence claim and either restate Fair-SMW as solving the fair-constrained minimization of Tr(H^T G^{-1} H) (a different relaxation than (mainobj)) or replace U by an operator (e.g., the compression of G to null(F^T)) that actually solves (SMW1), which changes the algorithm.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical claim that Fair-SMW is a reformulation of the constrained spectral clustering problem (mainobj)/(SMW1) is unsupported and false in general; the algorithm enforces the fairness constraint (range(U) ⊂ null(F^T)) but optimizes a different objective. Empirical results are unaffected but the derivation linking the method to normalized cut collapses.
issues.title: False equivalence of the constrained problems (SMW1) and (SMW2): Z is not square, so Z^T G^{-1} Z ≠ (Z^T G Z)^{-1}
issues.why_classification: The central mathematical justification of the proposed method is a false equivalence; every resolution either abandons the advertised connection to the fair NCut relaxation or changes the algorithm, so no comparable version of the claim survives.

issues.failure_explanation: The augmented Lagrangian is written with a negative penalty term, so the derived subproblem has matrix G^{-1} - μFF^T, which for large μ is indefinite and rewards violating the constraint. The displayed problem (SMW3) then silently switches to G^{-1} + μFF^T, which is the operator needed for Theorem thm:added-1 and the SMW step. As written, (SMW3) does not follow from the preceding derivation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the standard augmented Lagrangian with +μ/2‖F^TH‖_F^2 (a penalty for minimization), which yields G^{-1} + μFF^T consistently, and carry the orthonormality constraint through the subproblem.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation of (SMW3) from the Lagrangian is internally inconsistent; the later steps (invertibility, SMW inverse, μ→∞ limit) rely on the '+' version.
issues.title: Sign inconsistency in the augmented Lagrangian derivation leading to (SMW3)
issues.why_classification: A local sign correction restores consistency and all downstream steps remain as stated.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $G_{rw}$ has real eigenvalues and is generalized positive definite. That is $\bm{x}^T G_{rw}\bm{x} >0$
Therefore the eigenvalues of $B=\frac{1}{2}(D^{-1}W+WD^{-1})$ belong in $[-1,1]$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the numerical range of the non-normal matrix D^{-1}W by its spectral radius, which is invalid; the symmetric part B can have eigenvalues outside [-1,1] (for the 3-vertex path, B has eigenvalues ±(3/4)√2 ≈ ±1.06). The theorem itself fails: for a star with 16 leaves, x = (-4 at the center, 1 at each leaf) gives x^T D^{-1} W x = 17·(-4) = -68 and 2‖x‖² = 64, so x^T G_rw x = -4 < 0. (The statement also asserts strict positivity while the proof only argues ≥ 0.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the shift 2 by a shift c exceeding the numerical radius of D^{-1}W (e.g., c > sqrt(d_max/d_min), since |x^T D^{-1}W x| ≤ ‖D^{-1/2}x‖‖D^{1/2}x‖), or restrict the theorem to graphs where that bound is at most 2, and adjust the [1,3] spectral claims accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The RW variant loses its positivity guarantee: Theorem thm:added-1's hypothesis (x^T G^{-1} x > 0) and invertibility of F^T G_rw F are not ensured for G_rw, so the SMW-based construction of U_rw may be ill-defined on graphs with large degree disparity.
issues.title: Theorem thm:added-4 is false: G_rw = D^{-1}W + 2I is not generalized positive definite in general
issues.why_classification: The stated result is false but a contained fix (degree-dependent shift or hypothesis) restores a comparable RW variant with a new short argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $D^{-1}$ is an invertible diagonal matrix, it is of full rank, and multiplying by it from the right does not change the row space $ \mathcal{R}(F^T D^{-1}) = \mathcal{R}(F^T) $
We notice that $\mathcal{W}P$ is symmetric. Then we have that $$U_{\text{rw}}= D^{-1}\mathcal{W}P = D^{-1/2}D^{-1/2}\mathcal{W}PD^{-1/2}D^{1/2}$$

issues.failure_explanation: Right-multiplication by an invertible matrix preserves the column space, not the row space, of F^T; the identity requires range(D^{-1}F) ⊂ range(F), which fails unless degrees are constant within groups. Counterexample: path v1-v2-v3 (degrees 1,2,1), groups {v1,v2},{v3}, F=(1/2,1/2,-1): D^{-1}F=(1/2,1/4,-1) while P_F D^{-1}F ≈ (0.458,0.458,-0.917). Hence the simplification P = I - F(F^T𝒲F)^{-1}F^T𝒲 and the claimed similarity of U_rw to the symmetric matrix D^{-1/2}𝒲PD^{-1/2} are unjustified; realness of the eigenvalues of U_rw is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a new proof (e.g., via the pencil 𝒲y = λ D P y or U_rw = Z(Z^T 𝒲^{-1} D Z)^{-1} Z^T) or restrict the theorem to hypotheses under which the identity holds (degrees constant within each group), and otherwise treat the RW variant as heuristic.
issues.overall_effect: The RW variant's spectral well-posedness (real eigenvalues, hence meaningful 'largest eigenvalues' in Algorithm alg:smw-cluster with G_rw) is unproven.
issues.title: Proof of Theorem thm:added-5 relies on a false identity F^T D^{-1} = F^T D^{-1} F (F^T F)^{-1} F^T
issues.why_classification: The theorem's proof is invalid and a genuinely new argument or added hypothesis is required, but the impact is confined to one variant and the rest of the paper does not depend on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \State Construct the fairness-adjusted matrix $U_{\text{sym}} = G_{\mathrm{sym}} - M (F^T M)^{-1} F^T G_{\mathrm{sym}}$

issues.failure_explanation: With M = G^{-1}F the constructed matrix G - G^{-1}F(F^TG^{-1}F)^{-1}F^TG is neither symmetric nor annihilates F (UF = GF - G^{-1}F(F^TG^{-1}F)^{-1}F^TGF ≠ 0 in general), so its top eigenvectors need not satisfy F^T H = 0 and the fairness guarantee of the derivation is lost. The derivation requires M = GF.

failure_location.quote: \State Compute the projection matrix $M = G_{\mathrm{sym}}^{-1} F$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Set M = G_sym F in step 2 so that U_sym = G - M(F^TM)^{-1}F^TG matches the derivation.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the pseudocode does not implement the derived operator U and does not enforce the fairness constraint.
issues.title: Algorithm Fair-SMW computes M = G^{-1}F, inconsistent with the derived U = G - GF(F^TGF)^{-1}F^TG
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol local correction, identifiable from the derivation, restores the intended algorithm without loss.

issues.failure_explanation: The chain of inequalities establishes only an upper bound of 2. The supremum equals 2 exactly when the graph is bipartite; e.g., for the triangle the largest eigenvalue of L_sym is 3/2 < 2. The displayed equality is therefore false in general and unsupported by the proof.
issues.overall_effect: Only the stated equality is wrong; the bound λ(L_sym) ≤ 2 actually used in Theorems thm:added-2 and thm:added-4 is established.
issues.title: Theorem thm:added-7 asserts the supremum equals 2, but the proof only shows ≤ 2 and equality fails for non-bipartite graphs
issues.why_classification: A trivial local weakening of the statement to what the proof shows suffices; all uses need only the inequality.
